  ├────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ B. Only take focus when the    │ mouse users unaffected, keyboard │ most code                                                                │
  │ keyboard opened it             │  users get in                    │                                                                          │
  ├────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ C. Reuse the existing focus    │ reuses what's already there      │ pulls the caret into a card that appeared under your moving mouse — I'd  │
  │ manager                        │                                  │ not ship this                                                            │
  └────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  My recommendation: A. I confirmed in Chrome that it works in both directions with zero focus code. The only risk left is visual, and that's one
  browser pass to settle. If it looks fine, that's the whole fix.

  But there's a prior question, and it's the one I'd actually ask you: do you want readers Tabbing into these cards at all? A defensible alternative
  is to leave the card mouse-only and make it keyboard-inert — you'd not be able to open it with a keyboard either, so nothing is half-reachable.
  That's less correct by the accessibility rule, but it doesn't add a Tab stop to every link in the article. I've not built either.

  ---

  3. A small one, while you're deciding

  If a reader types half an annotation and then deliberately closes Annotate — should the draft survive? Right now it's lost. I noticed it while
  working on Escape and left it alone, because "deliberately closed" arguably means "meant to discard". Yes/no; either is a small change.

  ---

  Everything else that could be done without you is done and pushed.
